samples.summary: `shift` writes indent spaces directly after a `>` that has no trailing space, so the effective (CommonMark) indent is one column short — `prefixOf` output does not re-parse to the parts it was built from
samples.evidence: `QUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/` deliberately absorbs the one optional space CommonMark consumes after `>`. For a line written `>- b` the parse yields `quote='>'`, `indent=''`. Indenting under `>- a` gives `step = contentColumn(above) = 2`, and `prefixOf({...p, indent:'  '})` emits `'>' + '  ' + '- b'` → `>  - b`. Re-parsing that line (and CommonMark itself) consumes the first space as part of the quote marker, so the effective indent is 1, not the 2 that was needed to nest under the item above: the item does not actually nest, and the next `canIndent`/`indentList` pass sees indent 1 and shifts again. The invariant `parse(prefixOf(p)) === p` holds only when the quote already ends in a space.

samples.summary: Ordered-list counters are keyed by quote depth, so two *separate* blockquotes at the same depth inside one selection share a counter and the second one continues the first one's numbering
samples.evidence: `const level = `${quoteDepth(p)}:${p.indent.length}`` treats every line with one `>` as the same list. For a selection covering `> a`, `text`, `> b` (two distinct blockquotes separated by a paragraph), toggleOrderedList produces `> 1. a`, `1. text`, `> 2. b` — the second quote renders as a first item but is numbered 2. This is the same class of mis-numbering the hunk's own comment says it fixes for the inner/outer case; `itemAbove`/`parentOf` correctly stop the walk at a depth change, but the counter map has no such container boundary.

samples.summary: `setTaskChecked` silently no-ops for quoted tasks whose quote prefix `QUOTE_RE` cannot fully peel, while the preview renders those same items as live, clickable checkboxes
samples.evidence: `QUOTE_RE` only accepts one space per `>`, so `>  > - [ ] a` / `>    > - [ ] a` parse as `quote='> '`, `indent=' '`/`'   '`, `content='> - [ ] a'`, `check===null`, and `setTaskChecked` returns at line 378. markdown-it does render those as a nested blockquote task list (1–3 spaces then `>` is a valid nested quote), so the preview emits an enabled checkbox with a `data-source-line`; `onTaskClick` (preview.ts:322) has already called `preventDefault()`, so the click reverts visually and nothing is written — a silent failure on an interactive control. `hasUnpeeledQuote` guards the toggle/shift path but there is no equivalent guard or fallback here.

samples.summary: The quote-depth guard in `itemAbove`/`parentOf` also stops at a *deeper* quoted block that is content of the item above, producing a false `canIndent === false`
samples.evidence: `if (quoteDepth(prev) !== quoteDepth(p)) return null;` returns null for any depth mismatch, including a deeper one. For `> - a` / `> > nested quote inside a` / `> - b`, indenting `- b` walks up, hits depth 2 and bails, so `canIndent` is false even though `- b` is a legitimate sibling of `- a`. Skipping deeper-depth lines (as blank lines are skipped) would be the symmetric rule.

samples.summary: `shift`'s new early return skips the `view.focus()` that `replacePrefixes` always performed
samples.evidence: `if (!top) return;` returns before `replacePrefixes`, which ends with `view.focus()` even when it makes no changes. Both current callers only call `shift` after computing a non-zero step from a marker line, so the branch should be unreachable today; if it ever becomes reachable the editor silently loses focus restoration.

samples.summary: An empty task item still gets no accessible name, the case the new code exists to fix
samples.evidence: `if (name) box.setAttribute('aria-label', name);` — for `- [ ] ` (empty item, which the repo explicitly supports elsewhere via `listEmptyBulletPlugin`) `taskItemText` returns `''`, so no `aria-label` is written and the checkbox is announced as bare "checkbox". A positional fallback would close the gap.

finding.summary: Removing the `quoted` skip leaves deeply-indented / tab-indented blockquote lines unprotected, so a toggle writes a marker in front of the `>` again
finding.evidence: The old guard used `QUOTED_RE = /^\s*>/` and `replacePrefixes` skipped any matching line. The new `QUOTE_RE = /^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/` only recognises a quote after at most three *spaces*, and the `if (p.quoted) continue;` skip in `replacePrefixes` was deleted (list-commands.ts:229-237). A line such as `\t> quote` or `    > quote` (a blockquote nested inside a list item, which the editor can produce) now parses with `quote === ''`, `marker === ''`, `content === '> quote'`, and `toggleBulletList` rewrites its prefix to `indent + '- '`, producing exactly the `- > quote` corruption the previous commit's comment says it was avoiding. Nothing else guards this path: `shift`, `toggleKind` and `replacePrefixes` all now write unconditionally.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the quoted-line skip was removed from `replacePrefixes` and that nothing guards deeply/tab-indented blockquote lines. The skip is present at list-commands.ts:256 (`if (hasUnpeeledQuote(p)) continue;`), renamed rather than deleted, with `hasUnpeeledQuote` defined at :111-113 as `!p.marker && p.content.startsWith('>')`. Tracing the reviewer's own examples through parseLine (:49-74): `\t> quote`, `    > quote` and `>    > quote` all yield marker='' and content beginning with '>', so all three are skipped, not rewritten. Contrary to "shift, toggleKind and replacePrefixes all now write unconditionally", toggleKind (:293) and shift (:345) write exclusively via replacePrefixes and thus inherit the skip; the only other writer, setTaskChecked, returns early when `p.check === null` (:378), and a non-null check implies a LIST_RE marker, which hasUnpeeledQuote excludes. Tests at list-commands.test.ts:49-67 assert the exact non-corruption behaviour for these inputs. The code is not as described, so the claimed `- > quote` corruption cannot occur on this path.
